source.older_echium_reference: Impact of introduced honey bees on native pollination interactions of the endemic Echium wildpretii on Tenerife

question: Does the 2007-2009 Teide beehive perturbation provide visitor-specific direct per-visit effectiveness E_k on the same plant/context hierarchy as visit rates and reproductive outcomes?
reason: The primary perturbation study measures network visit frequencies and reproductive consequences but not visitor-specific single-visit effectiveness. Older Teide pollination studies cannot be transported across years/designs to manufacture E_k under the frozen mapping contract.
reopen_rule: Reopen only on a source-native artifact from the same 2007-2009 plant/context hierarchy that contains visitor-specific direct effectiveness, or on a prospective repeated Teide design measuring V_k and E_k together.
claim_boundary: This blocks only the narrow rate-weighted effective-service mapping. It does not weaken the Canary branching state-class result.
